thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity GPU runtime error detected on cluster 'inference-prod' — node=gpux-12 region=us-west-2 metric=cuda_error count=18
mei (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` from the runtime logs, multiple containers on gpux-12.
anna (sre): Copying recent dmesg excerpt:
anna (sre): ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4321, GPU error: 0x40c2
[ 12345.679012] kernel: gpu_mmu: Pagewalk error: misaligned address 0x7ffd3c000 at vpn 0x1f3
[ 12346.001234] container runtime: Illegal memory access (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS)
```
raj (eng-runtime): Looks like a pagewalk/misaligned translation. We saw a similar race in the page-table refactor branch but it was supposed to be gated. Could be driver+kernel+workload alignment.
luis (ml-eng): Affected pods are serving the large-context config (seq_len 4096) — heavy KV-cache usage.
carla (support): Support ticket queue: 6 customers have reported 502s or stalls; two are on Dedicated plans. Notifying CS.
mei (oncall): Triage plan: 1) drain node gpux-12, 2) scale up new nodes and rebalance, 3) failover traffic to cpu-fallback variant for impacted routes. Anyone see downside?
sarah (platform): Draining now will evict pods; latency may spike for those with large KV cache reloads. We should reduce batch size before draining to limit regen overhead.
anna (sre): Executing cordon+drain. Command:`kubectl cordon gpux-12 && kubectl drain gpux-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30`
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline paused for models: reroute-rule for /v1/generate updated to prefer cpu-fallback variant (canary)
raj (eng-runtime): Patching router to apply fallback for 10% initially, then 100% for routes associated with the failing model:`http PATCH https://router.internal/api/routes {"match":"model:open-lx-8b","priority_fallback":"cpu-fallback","weight":10}`
luis (ml-eng): cpu-fallback has quantized smaller KV memory so regen is faster but quality drop is ~3-4% on eval set. Will watch.
mei (oncall): Anna let me know when drain completes. Also collect kernel oops, coredumps, container logs for postmortem.
anna (sre): Drain initiated. Evicting pods, restarting kubelet on gpux-12 after warm reboot to clear driver state.
anna (sre): While draining, I see another worker hit the same error on gpux-15. Suspect a rolling propagation due to a common driver/kernel combo.
raj (eng-runtime): If it's driver+kernel, rollback kernel patch on nodes that upgraded in last 24h? Which nodes have that flag?
sarah (platform): Filtering nodes with kernel version 6.5.2 and nvidia-driver 535.43.02: gpux-12, gpux-15, gpux-19 are in that cohort.
carla (support): Customer impact update: 8 customers affected now, 2 seeing request spikes -> CS has opened refunds/credits where SLA breached.
luis (ml-eng): Quick mitigation: reduce max_seq to 2048 for live traffic to avoid deep KV walks. Can we patch request-time limit?
raj (eng-runtime): We can rewrite the request adaptor to clamp max_seq for that model route. Patching now:`PATCH /adaptor/config {"model":"open-lx-8b","max_seq_override":2048}`
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 50 minutes: next oncall is @sarah (platform).
mei (oncall): Anna status?
anna (sre): gpux-12 drained successfully and cordoned; kubelet restart completed. gpux-15 cordon in progress. No core dumps yet, capturing stacks and saving to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2428765432/*.
raj (eng-runtime): We're seeing a spike in Xid errors during model reloads (KV cache warmups). Hypothesis: concurrent pagewalks racy with new pte invalidation path. Need to throttle parallel loads.
luis (ml-eng): Throttling config applied: concurrent_warmups=2 for the serving runtime.
carla (support): Noting impacted customers and sending status update: "We're seeing degraded availability for some inference requests; mitigation in progress; ETA 30-45m for full recovery."
anna (sre): Kernel oops pushed to infra channel and attached to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2428765432/logs
raj (eng-runtime): Root-cause candidate: a race in the pagewalk fastpath introduced by kernel backport + new NV driver behaviour; manifests as misaligned virtual-to-physical translation causing illegal memory loads.
sarah (platform): Ops decision: schedule rolling rollback of nvidia-driver to 535.19 on the affected cohort, start with gpux-12/15/19, monitor Xid rate. Rollback window starting now, targeted 6 nodes per hour.
anna (sre): Rolling driver rollback in progress. Reboots required after package swap. Using graceful drain pattern to limit regen churn.
mei (oncall): Any immediate customer-facing blocking issues? Carla?
carla (support): Two customers on Dedicated want extended credits; legal loop engaged. Non-Dedicated customers mostly transient.
